design:
**Concrete blocker, small fix, unusually high leverage.** Not an epic — this is
a discrete piece of work that unblocks large parts of two programmes.

## The defect

`columns::model::ColumnType` has four variants:

```rust
pub enum ColumnType {
    DistillationColumn,   // condenser + reboiler
    AbsorptionColumn,     // neither; both end duties are user input
    ReboiledAbsorber,     // reboiler only
    RefluxedAbsorber,     // condenser only
}
```

There is **exactly one constructor**: `RigorousColumn::distillation`
(`columns/initial_estimates.rs:117`). **Three of the four column types are
unreachable from the public API.**

The solver already handles them — the enum, the duty back-calculation rules and
the docs all exist. Only the way in is missing.

## What this blocks

| unreachable variant | blocks |
|---|---|
| `RefluxedAbsorber` | a structurally correct CDU (a real CDU is a refluxed absorber, steam-stripped) |
| `AbsorptionColumn` | acid-gas removal; cracked-gas absorbers; TGTU absorption |
| `ReboiledAbsorber` | side strippers; reformate stabilizer; sour-water stripper |

That is the CDU (#82), AGR (#90), TGTU (#92), the cracked-gas recovery train,
BTX recovery, and the reformate stabilizer — **all waiting on constructors for
machinery that already works.**

## Why this is the pattern, again

This is the fourth programme running where the finding is **the data model
exists, the access seam is missing** (#58, #63, #70, #77). It is also the
single cheapest item in either programme relative to what it unblocks.

## Work

- Add constructors reaching the other three variants, matching
  `distillation`'s shape and documenting the duty convention each implies.
- Doc example per constructor, so the semantics are executable rather than
  asserted — the absorber's "both end duties are user input" rule is exactly
  the kind of thing that is silently got wrong.
- Regression test per variant.
- Export from the prelude when the crate gets one (it currently has none).

**Fidelity target: Crude estimate (API exposure only — no new physics).**
title: Expose the three unreachable ColumnType variants (absorber, reboiled, refluxed)

description:
Follow-up from op-nik1 (2026-08-11). The plenum stagnation inflow BC is verified for the single-phase subcooled steady path (Bernoulli-limit test in multiphase_1d/tests.rs, rel. error 1.12e-6) and exercised two-phase only indirectly via the Marviken gates (op-ja3t). Remaining direct-verification gaps, all stated in the test doc and the ReservoirInlet V&V block:
1. upwind_scalar (drift_flux.rs ~line 1504) has no direct unit test — it is private to drift_flux and multiphase_1d/tests.rs is a SIBLING module, so a direct test needs a pub(super) visibility change first (small code change, deliberately not made by the 2026-08-11 verification agents whose mandate was doc-only on drift_flux.rs).
2. Two-phase inflow: InflowState::void_fraction and rho_g were never exercised by a direct test (alpha = 0 exactly throughout the Bernoulli case).
3. The h0 - u^2/2 static-enthalpy split was only probed at ~2e-4 relative head; a higher-velocity case would test it meaningfully.
4. Backflow through either boundary and transient (non-steady) BC behaviour remain unverified.
Also noted, informational: the wall-friction closure applies Blasius at Re ~ 4.1e6, beyond its nominal ~1e5 range — reproduced, not corrected, by the verification test.
title: tampines: drift-flux inflow BC — residual verification gaps (upwind_scalar direct test, two-phase inflow, backflow)

description:
Follow-up found while finishing op-szai, measured against the hand-verified records in crates/kovan-literature/proprietary/papers/.

Both HTR-10 Elsevier papers still import with doi: null, but the correct DOI is mechanically derivable from data the extractor already reads and currently only *discards*:

  wu2002htr10.pdf   Info /Title = 'PII: S0029-5493(02)00182-6'
                    reference JSON doi = 10.1016/S0029-5493(02)00182-6
  gao2002htr10th.pdf Info /Title = 'PII: S0029-5493(02)00198-X'
                    reference JSON doi = 10.1016/S0029-5493(02)00198-X

i.e. DOI = '10.1016/' + PII, the standard Elsevier serial-item convention. metadata.rs already rejects the PII string as a title (is_title_junk / TITLE_JUNK_MARKERS 'pii:'), so the parse site exists; it just needs to keep the value instead of dropping it, and only when find_doi() found nothing in the front matter.

Not done under op-szai because it was outside that bead's stated scope (title/authors/document_type/sha256/slug) and it introduces a publisher-specific inference — 10.1016 is asserted to be Elsevier — which deserves the maintainer's sign-off rather than being slipped in. Verifiable immediately against the two committed reference JSONs.
title: kovan-literature: derive Elsevier DOIs from the PII in the PDF Info /Title
